newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia court case involving Megawati postponed.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia court case involving Megawati postponed.

text.p: An Indonesian judge on Thursday adjourned hearing a lawsuit filed by ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri against the government and military as her supporters faced eviction from their new headquarters.

Judge I Gde Ketut Sukarata adjourned Megawati's suit over her removal as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) by a government-backed faction after the defence questioned the court's jurisdiction.
"The court is adjourned until October 10...when we will hand down a decision on whether this court has the authority to hear this case," the judge said.

Municipal authorities meanwhile have given members of Megawati's PDI faction until Thursday evening to close the office they recently set up in a two-storey house in suburban East Jakarta after being evicted from the main headquarters.
Her supporters said they would refuse to obey the order and were preparing to sue the East Jakarta mayor, who said the office broke residential zoning laws.

During the five-minute court hearing, Megawati's supporters among about 200 people in the hot and crowded room jeered when the adjournment was announced. Scores of riot police around the court complex later peacefully dispersed about 200 demonstrators.
Megawati's chief lawyer, R.O. Tambunan, said her legal team would await the judge's decision but he said they believed the court did have the authority to hear the case.
Tambunan said government defence lawyers had said in a written reply to the plaintiff's arguments that the dispute was an internal matter of the PDI and not for the court to rule on.

Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, filed the suit against the government, the military and party rivals after PDI rebels ousted her from the party leadership at a special government-financed congress in June.
Megawati's sacking led to an unusual wave of dissent against the government, culminating in a police raid on PDI headquarters on July 27 in which her supporters were evicted from the building.
This triggered the worst riots in Jakarta in more than two decades.
Tambunan said lawyers for Megawati, who is still a member of parliament, were also preparing another suit against the committee organising general elections in late May next year.

Officials of the General Election Institute (LPU) have refused to accept a list of electoral candidates from Megawati's supporters after accepting a list from the new government-backed PDI leader, Surjadi.
The PDI, the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only parties allowed to contest the elections.
